description:
About the Position

The Loke Centre for Trophoblast Research at the University of Cambridge offers a 4-year fixed-term PhD studentship in placental biology. The studentship is based within the Centre's network of laboratories spanning the Department of Physiology, Development and Neuroscience and clinical departments, and provides an annual stipend of GBP 22,000 together with payment of university fees for the full four years. Research at the Centre addresses how the placenta develops and functions in health and disease, with implications for pregnancy complications such as fetal growth restriction and pre-eclampsia.

The successful candidate will join a research environment that integrates cell and organoid models, human placental tissue studies and advanced imaging to investigate trophoblast development and function. Students in the Centre benefit from dedicated supervision, core facilities and a vibrant community of reproductive scientists, and the studentship is designed to carry the student through to a completed PhD with conference travel and training support.

Research Environment and Application

Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain, a master's or outstanding bachelor's degree in a relevant life-science discipline such as developmental biology, cell biology, physiology, biomedical sciences or medicine. Applications are made through the University of Cambridge job board listing, with shortlisting by the Centre's project supervisors. The Loke Centre is one of the few dedicated trophoblast research centres worldwide, and its alumni now hold faculty positions internationally, making this studentship a strong entry point into reproductive biology research.

Highlights

  • 4-year fixed-term PhD studentship in placental biology
  • GBP 22,000 annual stipend plus university fees
  • Dedicated trophoblast research centre at Cambridge
  • Organoid, tissue and advanced-imaging approaches
  • Supervision across preclinical and clinical departments
  • Conference travel and research training support
